summary: A cap-one product quadratic family with nonzero spectrum {1,-1} has a literal physical cut with ||N||_F^2=25/32, e2(N^T N)=49/4096, row/column determinant-law disjointness >=13/28, and the completed E2 theorem gives H_{1/2}<17.015, yet the output density diverges logarithmically at zero. Therefore finite E2 half-Riesz credit alone cannot imply L-infinity; the third target spectral direction must be spent jointly. This is not a QFORM counterexample because the family has only two large eigenvalues.
